questions.question: The terms "objects" and "oriented", in the sense of object-oriented programming, made their first appearance in what institution?

choices.statement: MIT - late 1950s and early 1960s
Stanford - late 1940s and early 1950s
Harvard - late 1960s and early 1970s
UC Berkley - mid 1950s

questions.hint: Think of a famous technology institute in Massachusetts, around the late 1950s.

questions.question: In Java, a variable declared using a class type, such as Circle c1;, is best described as which of the following?

choices.statement: A primitive variable that stores the object's data directly in its own memory space
A reference variable that stores the address of an object
An object that has already been instantiated
A constant that cannot be reassigned

questions.hint: It holds an address, not the object itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of a Java constructor?

choices.statement: It has the same name as its class and has no return type, not even void
It must have a return type of void
It must be invoked explicitly by name, like any other method
A class may have only one constructor

questions.hint: It is named after its class and has no return type at all.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a class from an object?

choices.statement: A class is a runtime instance, While an object is the template used to create it
A class and an object are the same thing in Java
A class is an extensible template, and an object is an instance of exactly one class
An object may be an instance of several unrelated classes at the same time

questions.hint: One is the blueprint; the other is something built from it.

questions.question: A class declares its constructors as follows. What happens when the class defines at least one constructor, none of which takes zero parameters?

choices.statement: Java still supplies a default constructor automatically
Java does not supply a default constructor automatically
The class cannot be compiled
The first constructor is automatically treated as the default constructor

questions.hint: Once you write any constructor yourself, Java stops providing one for free.

questions.question: Which access modifier allows a member to be accessed by subclasses, while still preventing direct access from unrelated class outside the package?

choices.statement: private
public
protected
static

questions.hint: It sits between private and public: subclasses can see it.

questions.question: A subclass defines a public method with the same name, parameter list, and return type as a public method in its superclass. This is known as:

choices.statement: Method overloading
Method overriding
Shallow copying
Encapsulation

questions.hint: Same signature in the subclass, but new behavior.

questions.question: Which statement about abstract classes in Java is correct?

choices.statement: An abstract class cannot contain constructors or instance variables
A class containing an abstract method may be declared non-abstract
An abstract class cannot be instantiated, but a reference variable of its type can be declared
A subclass of an abstract class can always be instantiated, even if it leaves inherited abstract methods undefined

questions.hint: You cannot create one directly, but you can still declare variables of its type.

questions.question: Java does not allow a class to extend more than one class. Which mechanism does Java provide to simulate multiple inheritance?

choices.statement: Allowing a class to implement multiple interfaces
Declaring all methods static
Using the final modifier on classes
Overloading constructors

questions.hint: A class can extend only one class, but it can do this with many of the other kind of type.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of method headings in the same class correctly overloads a method?

choices.statement: public void calc(int x, double y) and public int calc(int x, double y)
public void calc(int x, double y) and public void calc(double y, int x)
public void calc(int x) and public void calc(int y)
public int calc(int x) and public double calc(int x)

questions.hint: Overloads need different parameter lists; the return type does not count.

public boolean equals(Object o) { return this == o; }
public boolean equals(Object o) { return false; }
public boolean equals(Object o) { return o instanceof Item && ((Item) o).id.equals(id); }
